text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- SERBIA --
NASA BORBA
- Protesting war invalids reached an agreement with the government to be paid outstanding disability pensions and start receiving regular payments by September.

- The procedure for electing Yugoslav president will start within a few days and will be completed by July 25, said deputy speaker of the Upper House of the Yugoslav parliament Radmilo Bogdanovic. He said the Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) would withdraw its initiative for constitutional changes for the time being.
- The Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro will chose its presidential candidate by July 11.
- Newly elected governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia Dusan Vlatkovic promises to keep dinar stable.
- The federal parliament passed a package of laws on the economic system and adjustment of norms to the European Union.
- Head of the United Nations Transition Authority in Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein asked for extension of the UNTAES mandate until January 1997.

- Storms have damaged crops on at least 139,000 hectares, or 8.5 percent of the total area, in Vojvodina, Serbia's granary. The damage is estimated to cost at least 300 million dinars, but the harvest is expected to be higher than in 1996.
- Leader of Democratic Party (DS) Zoran Djindjic says the DS will not agree to an increase in the number of electoral units and that accepting nine electoral units had already been a compromise.
POLITIKA

- Works on Nis-Pristina-Pec-Cakor-Matesevo-Podgorica-Misici highway, an integral part of the international highway E-80, will start in March 1998. The stretch is 374 kilometres long (222 in Serbia and 152 in Montenegro).
- Yugoslav parliament elected Vukasin Jokanovic, Yugoslav Interior Minister, as the federal state prosecutor.
- This year's wheat harvest expected to be 2.75 million tonnes substantially up on the 1.5 million tonnes last year. Farmers call government to determine guaranteed price of wheat.
- Telekom Srbija held its founding shareholders' meeting and elected members of the board of directors headed by Milorad Vucelic, SPS vice-president.
DEMOKRATIJA
- The problem with pension funds here and in other countries is the demographic trend; the funds cannot finance pensioners who now live longer, said Oskar Kovac a member of the SPS main board.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Financial inspectors estimate there are some 100,000 people in Serbia involved in illegal trade in goods.
- Bosnian Archbishop Vinko Puljic due to meet Serbian Orthodox Church Patriarch Pavle in Belgrade on July 9 or 10, sources say.
- Yugoslav parliament passes law on public holidays, which includes January 1/2 (New Year), April 27 (statehood day), May 1/2 (Labour Day), May 9 (Victory Day) and November 29/30 (Republic Day).
-- MONTENGRO --
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin government discussed the Montenegrin railways' 1996 annual report. The railways transported 2.5 times more goods than in 1995 while the number of passengers dropped by 27 percent.
- According to a poll conducted by Damar agency Montenegro's daily Pobjeda has 100,000 readers, Vecernje Novosti 75,293, Dnevni Telegraf 42,970, Politika 29,661 and Blic 23,957.
MONITOR
- Out of 1,000 people polled in eight municipalities 64.5 percent are against election of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic as federal president, according to Damar agency.
- My meeting with (Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo) Djukanovic can be regarded as the beginning of a new coalition said DS president Zoran Djindjic. -- Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 43 05
